Data sets for illustrating the functions in the SPEI package

Source: R/data.R
Datasets.Rd

Data used in the examples of the SPEI package: wichita dataset: monthly climate in Wichita (Kansas, lat=37.6475, elevation=402.6 m a.s.l.) from January 1980 to October 2011; balance dataset: monthly climatic water balance (precipitation minus potential evapotranspiration) at eleven locations around the World, since January 1900 (1296 months); cabinda: one year of data for computing Penman-Monteith ET0 from Allen et al. (1998); cruts4: 120 years of monthly climatic water balance (precipitation minus reference evapotranspiration) data at six grid points from CRU TS 4.05; tarazona: annual basal area increment of 18 cores of Aleppo pine (Pinus halepensis) at Tarazona (Spain) from 1959 to 2017, and climate at the same site with 48 periods per year (four per month) from 1961 to 2020.

Usage

data(wichita)
data(balance)
data(cabinda)
data(cruts4)
data(tarazona)

Format

wichita dataset: a data frame with:

YEAR

year.

MONTH

month of the year (1 to 12).

PRCP

monthly precipitation totals, in mm.

TMAX

monthly mean daily maximum temperature, in ºC.

TMIN

monthly mean daily minimum temperature, in ºC.

TMED

monthly mean temperature, in ºC.

AWND

monthly mean wind speed, in m s-1.

TSUN

monthly mean daily sunshine duration, in h. Note: five values between October 2000 and May 2001 (15.0 to 21.1 h) exceed the maximum possible day length at this latitude and should be treated with caution.

ACSH

monthly mean cloud cover, in %.

balance dataset: a data frame with monthly climatic water balance (precipitation minus potential evapotranspiration) at Indore (India), Kimberley (South Africa), Albuquerque (US), Valencia (Spain), Wien (Austria), Abashiri (Japan), Tampa (US), Sao Paulo (Brazil), Lahore (Pakistan), Punta Arenas (Chile) and Helsinki (Finland), in mm. cabinda dataset: a data frame with one year of monthly climatic data at Cabinda (Angola, -5.33S 12.11E 20 m), with:

mon

month of the year

Tmin

monthly mean daily minimum temperature, in ºC.

Tmax

monthly mean daily maximum temperature, in ºC.

RH

monthly mean relative humidity, in %.

U2

monthly mean wind speed at 2 m height, in m s-1.

tsun

monthly mean sunshine hours, in h.

Rs

monthly mean daily incoming solar radiation, MJ m-2 d-1.

ET0

monthly ET0 from the original publication, in mm.

cruts4 dataset: an array with 120 years of monthly climatic water balance (precipitation minus reference evapotranspiration) data at six grid points from CRU TS 4.05 data set. The array has dimensions [time=1440, longitude=2, latitude=3], with time starting in January 1900. Longitudes are (0.25, 0.75), and latitudes (42.25, 42.75, 43.25), corresponding to the Central Pyrenees between Spain and France.

tarazona dataset: a list with three elements, with data from the unthinned (control) plot of an Aleppo pine (Pinus halepensis) plantation at Tarazona (Zaragoza, Spain; lat=41.8667, lon=-1.8333, elevation=785 m a.s.l.):

site

a list with the site metadata: name, lat, lon, elevation (m a.s.l.), species, plot (the plot code, TAPHD), treatment (control, i.e. unthinned) and thinning.year (1998, the year in which the neighbouring plots of the experiment were thinned; the control plot was not thinned).

bai

a data frame with the annual basal area increment (BAI, in cm2 per year) of the control plot. The first column, year, has the years (1959 to 2017), and the other 18 columns the BAI of each core, NA outside the years covered by the core. The cores come from 11 trees. The column names are the plot code, the tree number and the core letter, e.g. TAPHD06A and TAPHD06B are two cores of tree TAPHD06. BAI has an age and size trend, which must be removed before relating it to climate (see vignette("scale_scan")).

clim

a multivariate time series (ts) with frequency 48 (four periods per month), from the first period of January 1961 to the last period of December 2020 (2880 periods). The periods of each month start on days 1, 9, 16 and 23, so they span days 1-8, 9-15, 16-22, and 23 to the end of the month. The columns are PRCP, precipitation in mm per period; ETO, FAO-56 Penman-Monteith reference evapotranspiration in mm per period; TMIN and TMAX, mean daily minimum and maximum temperature in the period, in ºC. Values are rounded to two decimals.

Source

The wichita data were obtained from the Global Historical Climatology Network (GHCN, https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/). Data for the balance dataset were extracted from CRU TS V3.1 and from the 20th Century Reanalysis V2 data set. Data for the cabinda dataset were taken from Allen et al. (1998), page 69, figure 18. The cruts4 data were obtained from the CRU (Climatic Research Unit, University of East Anglia https://crudata.uea.ac.uk/) TS V4.05 data set. The basal area increment in the tarazona dataset comes from Manrique-Alba et al. (2020), and is part of the dataset: Manrique-Alba, À., Molina, A.J., Beguería, S., Camarero, J.J., et al. (2025). Basal Area Increment and Climate Data from Long-Term Silviculture Monitoring Sites in Spain (SilvAdapt.net) [Dataset]. DIGITAL.CSIC, doi:10.20350/digitalcsic/17165 . The same data were used in Manrique-Alba et al. (2025). The climate data were extracted from the gridded dataset of the Spanish drought monitor (https://monitordesequia.csic.es, Vicente-Serrano et al., 2017). The tarazona data are distributed with the package, under its licence (GPL (>= 2)), by the data authors. The script used to build the dataset is data-raw/tarazona.R in the package source repository.

R.G. Allen, L.S. Pereira, D. Raes, M. Smith. 1998. Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements - FAO Irrigation and drainage paper 56. FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

À. Manrique-Alba, S. Beguería, A.J. Molina, M. González-Sanchis, M. Tomàs-Burguera, A.D. del Campo, M. Colangelo, J.J. Camarero. 2020. Long-term thinning effects on tree growth, drought response and water use efficiency at two Aleppo pine plantations in Spain. Science of the Total Environment 728: 138536, DOI: 10.1016/j.scitotenv.2020.138536.

À. Manrique-Alba, S. Beguería, J.J. Camarero, A.J. Molina, et al. 2025. Adaptive responses to thinning: growth and sensitivity to hydric and thermal stress in four widely planted pine species. Agricultural and Forest Meteorology 373: 110777, DOI: 10.1016/j.agrformet.2025.110777.

S.M. Vicente-Serrano, M. Tomas-Burguera, S. Beguería, F. Reig, B. Latorre, M. Peña-Gallardo, M.Y. Luna, A. Morata, J.C. González-Hidalgo. 2017. A high resolution dataset of drought indices for Spain. Data 2(3): 22, DOI: 10.3390/data2030022.
